title: RWB-S8-E7010-APP: the contact-breach path has no rule row, no column, no published ledger read, no operation of its own, no event and no write right for its primary role
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7010-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 8 and 13); legacy RWB-E7-010; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.19 and Requirements served; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01, R-DEV-20 and R-UNI-10 to R-UNI-44; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 deviation, interaction and LOV-CONDUCT; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-06 and EV-07; Feature List v4 FEAT-OCC-05, FEAT-OCC-06 and FEAT-DVF-10; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-DVH-004 and REQ-DVH-011
description: (1) No rule row of the DEV set of 22 rules or of the UNIVERSAL set of 50 rules names a contact sent while a contact stop is in force: the DEV set carries contact rules only for X6 (R-DEV-16, R-DEV-17), the UNIVERSAL set carries the stop itself (R-UNI-04 to R-UNI-06), the conduct hold (R-UNI-10) and the lift (R-UNI-44), and R-LIT-22 CONDUCT_CHECK_FAILED is a litigation rule over one notice. The rule that opens the breach path therefore has no ID, and the story evaluates R-UNI-39 and R-DEV-20 instead of inventing one. (2) No column of deviation carries a breach, a breach handler or a breach clock: TSD S8 T3.1 gives ten fields, DF-CAS-042 holds one handler and no field holds a second, and the story therefore writes no column of its own table. (3) The interaction ledger is rwb-source-data's by the R3 default ruling and no source publishes an operation that reads its outbound contacts, so the consumed row carries a placeholder and DP-18 is not in the plan's pattern set. (4) The Ownership Map gives S8 exactly two REST operations, both of RWB-S8-E7001-APP, and no operation carries a breach, so the breach act has no published entry point and SCR-08's breach read is unpublished. (5) The service owns EV-06 DeviationRaised and EV-07 DeviationCleared and both belong to the raise and resolution story, so a breach has no event even though the connection matrix has rwb-comms listening to S8. (6) TSD S8 T6.1 gives RW-CONDUCT R on Case record only while FSD S8 A2.19.3.3 names the Conduct and QA officer primary and RW-COMPLY as also using, so the primary role cannot take the write the feature describes. (7) FSD S8 A2.19.1 sets the service level with DL22 while R-DEV-20's timer column carries 10 working days, so the clock length has two sources. (8) The plan gives H = RWB-S8-E7010-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the path consumes the rwb-source-data ledger and the rwb-case boundary. (9) The legacy Data table names timer, decision_log_entry and rule_row, three tables of other owners, and no table of its own beyond deviation. (10) EP07 is wave 4 and rwb-deviation is wave 2, so the business wave is later than the service wave and is kept as the plan gives it.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.19.1 to A2.19.4.3 (objective, one metric, three flow steps, VR-S8-019-1 and BR-S8-019, the eight deviation fields, the Conduct and QA officer primary and RW-COMPLY also using, AC-S8-019-01 and the two exception criteria); TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.2 (the ten deviation fields and the three lists); TSD S8 T4 (22 rules over 9 states, no contact-breach row); TSD S8 T6.1 (RW-CONDUCT R); TSD S8 T5.3 and Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-06 and EV-07 (DeviationRaised with caseId, deviationCode and raisedBy; DeviationCleared with caseId, deviationCode and outcome); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01, R-DEV-16, R-DEV-17, R-DEV-20, R-UNI-04 to R-UNI-06, R-UNI-10, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-44; LDM v8 interaction DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029 and LOV-CONDUCT PASSED, BLOCKED, NOT_APPLICABLE; Feature List v4 FEAT-OCC-06 (P6 blocks an outbound contact and leaves the message unsent) and FEAT-DVF-10 (RW-CONDUCT primary, RW-COMPLY secondary); context pack S8 ownership rows (one table, two operations, two events, no job, one workflow) and connection-matrix row S8 (E to P3, R and E to P1, T and E to P10, no row to P6); legacy RWB-E7-010 Data, Endpoints and Permission tables; split plan dependency rows of RWB-S8-E7010-APP.
area: Business rules, data model, API contract, events, access
owner_role: Center of excellence with the solution architect, the rwb-decision rule owner, the rwb-source-data owner and the rwb-access owner
proposed: Publish one UNIVERSAL rule row for a contact sent against a contact stop with its own ID and route it to the Conduct and QA officer; decide whether a breach is stored on deviation (a new field or a second record) or on the decision record only; publish the interaction-ledger read operation on rwb-source-data; publish the SCR-08 breach read; decide whether a breach publishes an event of its own; correct the RW-CONDUCT right in rwb-access; settle the service level with DL22 or take R-DEV-20's 10 working days as the one value. Until then the story evaluates the published rows, writes no column, publishes nothing and carries the placeholders.

title: RWB-S8-E7010-CON: the consumed ledger operation, the breach-entry attributes, the breach read, the conduct-officer right and the clock length have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7010-CON; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; legacy RWB-E7-010; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.19.3.1, A2.19.3.3, A2.19.4 and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01, R-DEV-20 and R-UNI-30 to R-UNI-44; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 interaction and LOV-CONDUCT; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 API-S8-001 and API-S8-002; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-DVH-004 and REQ-DVH-011
description: (1) No source publishes an operation that reads the outbound contacts of a case from the interaction ledger, so the one consumed row carries a placeholder and its owner is fixed only by the R3 default ruling. (2) The API Specification's two deviation operations are writes of the deviation itself and neither carries a breach, so the baseline declares no operation and the breach read behind SCR-08 is unpublished. (3) The breach-entry attributes have no schema of their own: the local record of DP-03 is a library object and no source fixes the names, the clock start or the escalation attribute, so the baseline proposes them and the library owner confirms. (4) TSD S8 T6.1 gives RW-CONDUCT R only while FSD S8 names the Conduct and QA officer primary, so the baseline must record a conflict rather than declare a right the matrix does not give. (5) The clock length has two sources: DL22 sets the target in FSD S8 A2.19.1 and R-DEV-20's timer column carries 10 working days, so the element declares reference data with a version and a placeholder. (6) No event exists for a breach: EV-06 and EV-07 are the raise and resolution of a deviation and belong to RWB-S8-E7001-APP. (7) The plan's C row is empty although the path consumes rwb-source-data and rwb-case, and DP-18 and DP-07 are not in the pattern set although the ledger and the lists of values are consumed.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.19.2 to A2.19.4.3 (integration point Workbench, prerequisites FEAT-OCC-06, VR-S8-019-1, BR-S8-019, the eight field-catalog rows, the two roles, the main and the two exception criteria, no background event); TSD S8 T2 (record the decision before the change), T3.0 (standard record columns), T3.1 and T3.2 (the ten fields and the three lists), T3.3 (one relationship to recovery_case), T4 (the 9 DEVIATION states), T5.2 (published interfaces of P3 to P7), T5.3 (DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared published), T6.1 (RW-CONDUCT R; the U holders) and T-A.1 (API-S8-001 and API-S8-002 on /api/recovery/v1, Case record U, Epic 2); LDM v8 interaction DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029 and LOV-CONDUCT; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01, R-DEV-20, R-UNI-30, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-44; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-06 and EV-07; context pack S8 ownership rows and connection-matrix row S8; legacy RWB-E7-010 Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks and Validation and messages.
area: API contract, data model, access, reference data, events
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner, the rwb-access owner, the platform library owner and Compliance
proposed: Publish the interaction-ledger read operation with its fields and its 2 s budget; confirm the breach-entry attributes against the local record schema; publish the SCR-08 breach read; record the RW-CONDUCT conflict and resolve it in the access matrix rather than in a contract; settle the service level with DL22; confirm that no breach event is published in wave 4. Until then the baseline declares the consumed row and the entry with the placeholders and the three absences.
